reason: This passage from Exodus 19 describes God's preparation of the people at Mount Sinai, including sanctification, boundary establishment, and Moses serving as an intermediary. There is no instance of the regular people complaining to their leaders in this text. Moses does report to God about the people's inability to ascend the mountain (v. 23), but this is Moses speaking to God, not the people complaining to their leader. The passage focuses on obedience to divine instructions and respect for sacred boundaries, not on the impropriety of complaints from people to leaders. No such moral is conveyed.
